_comment: Single source of truth for the Get Started guide. tests/test_site_commands.py runs every `provenant` command here against the real CLI, so keep them exact.

shells.label: PowerShell
shells.where: Start menu, type PowerShell, open Windows PowerShell (not as administrator).

shells.label: Command Prompt
shells.where: Start menu, type cmd, open Command Prompt.

shells.label: Terminal
shells.where: Your terminal emulator, as your normal user (no sudo).

methods.label: One-line installer
methods.what: Finds Python 3.10+, installs Provenant for your user only (no admin, no dependencies), adds a provenant command, then starts provenant setup, which shows a plan and asks before changing anything.
methods.note: Read the script first if you prefer: open the same URL in your browser.

methods.label: pipx
methods.what: Installs Provenant into its own isolated environment and puts provenant on your PATH. Needs pipx (python -m pip install --user pipx, then pipx ensurepath).

methods.label: pip (no PATH changes)
methods.what: Installs the wheel for your user with pip. You then run Provenant as a Python module, which works even when pip's scripts folder is not on PATH.

install.windows: Install Python from python.org/downloads (tick "Add python.exe to PATH") or run: winget install Python.Python.3.12
install.macos: Install Python from python.org/downloads, or with Homebrew: brew install python
install.linux: Use your package manager, for example: sudo apt install python3 python3-pip

clients.label: Claude Code
clients.status_note: Tested with a real Claude Code session: rm -rf and reading .env were blocked.
clients.connects: A PreToolUse / PostToolUse / UserPromptSubmit hook. Claude Code asks Provenant before every tool call, including built-in tools like Bash, Read and Write.
clients.changes: ~/.claude/settings.json (adds three hook entries; everything else is kept)
clients.restart: Start a new Claude Code session.

clients.label: Claude Desktop
clients.status_note: Local (stdio) MCP servers are routed through the Provenant proxy. Remote (HTTP) MCP servers are not proxied yet.
clients.connects: Each local MCP server entry is rewritten to start through the Provenant proxy, which checks every tools/call. The original entry is kept inside it.
clients.restart: Quit Claude Desktop completely (tray or menu bar icon, Quit), then open it again.

clients.label: Cursor
clients.status_note: Uses the same proxy and config rewrite, tested on sample configs only, not yet inside the Cursor app.
clients.connects: Each local MCP server in Cursor's global MCP config starts through the Provenant proxy.

clients.label: Windsurf
clients.status_note: Uses the same proxy and config rewrite, tested on sample configs only, not yet inside the Windsurf app.
clients.connects: Each local MCP server in Windsurf's MCP config starts through the Provenant proxy.

clients.label: Antigravity
clients.status_note: Google's agent IDE and CLI. Uses the same proxy and config rewrite as Cursor. The config path and format come from Google's Antigravity MCP docs; tested here only on sample configs, not inside the real Antigravity app. Remote (serverUrl) servers are not proxied yet.
clients.connects: Each local MCP server in Antigravity's global MCP config starts through the Provenant proxy.
clients.restart: Restart Antigravity (or refresh its MCP servers).

clients.label: Manual MCP config
clients.status_note: For any client that reads an mcpServers JSON file. Preview first with --dry-run.
clients.connects: Wraps every local MCP server in the config file you name.
clients.changes: The file you pass (a timestamped backup is written next to it)
clients.restart: Restart the client that reads that file.

expected: Read hello.txt (inside a temp folder): expected ALLOW
Reuse that grant for a different file: expected refused
Bash: rm -rf ~ (evaluated only; never executed): expected DENY
Check the canary file still exists: expected present
Bash: npm publish (evaluated only): expected REQUIRE_APPROVAL
Find these decisions in the audit log: 4 entries, chain intact

levels.label: Installed
levels.means: The provenant package runs on this machine. Nothing routes through it yet.

levels.label: Engine ready
levels.means: The policy loads and the audit chain verifies.

levels.label: Configured
levels.means: A client config or the Claude Code hook points at Provenant.

levels.label: Connected
levels.means: Provenant has seen at least one real tool call from that client.

levels.label: Verified
levels.means: provenant verify passed against your current policy.

model.status_text: No Provenant model is trained or hosted yet. Model assistance works with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you run or rent.

troubleshooting.title: 'python' or 'py' is not recognized
troubleshooting.means: No Python 3.10+ is installed, or it is installed but this terminal cannot find it.

fix.windows: Install Python from python.org/downloads and tick "Add python.exe to PATH" (or run: winget install Python.Python.3.12). Then open a new terminal.
fix.macos: Install Python from python.org/downloads or with: brew install python. Then open a new terminal.
fix.linux: Install it with your package manager, for example: sudo apt install python3 python3-pip

if_fails.windows: If 'py' still fails but 'python' opens the Microsoft Store, turn off the python.exe alias in Settings, Apps, Advanced app settings, App execution aliases, then reinstall from python.org.
if_fails.macos: Run the 'Install Certificates' and 'Update Shell Profile' scripts in /Applications/Python 3.x, then open a new terminal.
if_fails.linux: Check 'which python3'. Some distributions name it python3.12; use that name instead.

troubleshooting.title: 'provenant' is not recognized
troubleshooting.means: Provenant is installed, but pip put the provenant command in a folder that is not on PATH, or this terminal was opened before the install.

fix.windows: Open a new terminal. If it still fails, run Provenant as a module, which always works: py -m provenant
fix.macos: Open a new terminal. If it still fails, run Provenant as a module: python3 -m provenant
fix.linux: Open a new terminal. If it still fails, run Provenant as a module: python3 -m provenant

if_fails.windows: 'No module named provenant' means it was installed into a different Python. Install again with the same py command.
if_fails.macos: 'No module named provenant' means it was installed into a different Python. Install again with python3 -m pip.
if_fails.linux: 'No module named provenant' means it was installed into a different Python. Install again with python3 -m pip.

troubleshooting.title: The package installs but the command does not run
troubleshooting.means: A partial or mixed install: often an old 0.8.0 copy or an interrupted download.

if_fails.all: Run the same command with --json and open an issue on GitHub with its output. It never contains secrets.

troubleshooting.title: The downloaded .whl file is actually HTML
troubleshooting.means: The download link answered with a web page (usually a login page) instead of the package. 0.8.0's site link did this.

fix.all: Install straight from the GitHub URL in step 2, which serves the real file. Delete the bad .whl.

if_fails.all: False means the file is not a wheel. Compare its SHA-256 with SHA256SUMS.txt in the repository's dist folder.

troubleshooting.title: The download link redirects to a Vercel login page
troubleshooting.means: That deployment is protected by Vercel Authentication, so anonymous visitors get a sign-in page instead of the file.

fix.all: Use the GitHub download URL in step 2. It is public and serves the binary.

if_fails.all: The final Content-Type should be application/octet-stream. If it says text/html, tell us on GitHub.

troubleshooting.title: Setup does not find my AI client
troubleshooting.means: Setup reads the client's config file. The file does not exist until the client has run once with an MCP server configured.

fix.all: Open the client, add at least one MCP server in its settings, close it, then run setup again. Or choose Manual MCP config and pass the file path.

if_fails.all: Run doctor: it lists every config path it checked.

troubleshooting.title: An MCP server does not start after setup
troubleshooting.means: The wrapped entry starts the proxy with the Python that ran setup. If that Python or virtual environment moved or was deleted, the server cannot start.

fix.all: Undo and redo the change for that client: rollback --client CLIENT, then setup --client CLIENT.

if_fails.all: Open the client's MCP log (Claude Desktop: Settings, Developer, Open logs folder) and look for the provenant proxy line.

troubleshooting.title: The security test does not behave as expected
troubleshooting.means: Usually a customised ~/.provenant/policy.json changed a decision, or the policy file has an error.

fix.all: Check the policy for mistakes with: policy lint

if_fails.all: Rename ~/.provenant/policy.json temporarily so the built-in policy is used, and run verify again. If it then passes, the custom policy is the cause.

troubleshooting.title: Model inference is unavailable
troubleshooting.means: The endpoint is unreachable, the key is missing, or the model answered in the wrong format. Deterministic protection keeps working either way.

fix.all: Check the endpoint and whether the key variable is set (the key itself is never shown): model status

if_fails.all: Set "enabled": false in ~/.provenant/model.json. Your policy's model_assist.on_error decides whether calls wait for a human while the model is down.
